integrity: The foundational publication date and same-object mathematical classification were checked in bibliographic records. The complete Sprott–Chlouverakis article was inspected for the exact equations, bifurcation route, attractor statistics, conservative b=0 measure discussion, and symbolic dynamics. Relevant published critical-damping results were compared at statement and implication level and lie outside the accepted 0<b<1 domain. The conditional laws, speed defects, support bound, and equality rigidity were independently reconstructed from invariance and replayed with the packaged exact checker.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is a necessary stationary law for compactly supported invariant probability measures and does not prove existence or uniqueness of a physical measure.
The accepted domain is 0<b<1; the algebraic conditional identities extend further, but the claim is intentionally restricted to the nontrivial feedback regime below the critical damping threshold.
The conditional laws determine drive means and variance defects, not full conditional distributions.
A differently phrased elementary generator identity could remain in unindexed nonlinear-dynamics literature.
title: Exact stationary feedback calibration and speed defects in the Thomas cyclic flow
